what_it_does: G-SpNN tackles a problem in high-frequency circuit design: when engineers build machine-learning-based models (neural networks) to predict how electrical signals behave in circuits, these models can predict physically impossible results—signals that gain energy from nothing, violating passivity (energy conservation). Enforcing passivity traditionally requires complex optimization that consumes huge memory and converges slowly. G-SpNN reformulates this as a neural network training problem and runs it on GPUs, converting passivity constraints into regularization terms (soft penalties during learning) that the GPU can handle efficiently. This dramatically speeds convergence while reducing memory overhead.
